title.narrative: Food production support and integrated multi-sector emergency services in Tawila, North Darfur

description.narrative: ltpgtHumanitarian needs in North Darfur are critically high due to ongoing conflict and limited access to humanitarian aid, with particularly high needs identified in the locality of Tawilla. Vulnerable children and families face barriers to accessing healthcare, shelter and basic services due to the disruption of supplies, infrastructure damage, displacements, and imposed restrictions. As part of its ongoing humanitarian response program in North Darfur, SCI and partners Plan International, APDHWO and NADA propose a project that aims to reduce morbidity and mortality and to improve the living conditions and protection of displaced individuals and host communities in Tawilla. In line with the HRP and cluster objectives, the project will deliver safe, timely, principled and gender-responsive assistance to 74,417 people and target the most vulnerable population groups including women, men, children and persons with disabilities. ltbrgtUnder the leadership of SC, the Consortium will contribute to improving equitable and inclusive access to quality life-saving curative and preventative healthcare services to 24,041 people (6.171 specifically for nutrition) through two health facilities. To fill identified health and nutrition gaps including medical supplies, incentives, minor rehabilitation and referrals and increase the coverage, the project will target women of reproductive age, with a focus on pregnant and lactating women, and children under 5 years of age, while providing gender-sensitive and disability-inclusive lifesaving healthcare for communicable and non-communicable diseases among children over 5, adults and the elderly. The proposed health interventions will provide essential maternal and child health services, essential medication, and supplies (PPE, diagnostics, case management), establish referral pathways and strengthen the immunization services. SC will also provide emergency lifesaving nutrition services with an emphasis on increasing access for conflict-affected people in all targeted localities, including community management of acute malnutrition (CMAM) and preventive nutrition services. The project will secure nutrition supplies, contribute to facilities running cost, and establish linkages between stabilisation centres, OTP and TSFP sites. The Consortium will ensure that targeted health facilities are equipped with necessary WASH infrastructure and materials, including water purification systems, excreta disposal facilities, cleaning materials, and solid waste management systems. We will also ensure that targeted communities have access to safe WASH services including access to safe water, sanitation, proper waste management and hygiene promotion.ltbrgtUnder the Shelter/NFI component, Plan International will provide NFI and shelter to support essential daily activities and offer adaptable shelter solutions to 2,989 people. This will include life-saving in-kind non-food items to the most vulnerable IDPs and host communities, distribute cash for shelter/NFIs to assist affected households to establish or rehabilitate shelters, supply and construct emergency shelter with high-standards and provide materials for the construction of emergency shelter.lt/pgtltpgtA total of 3,475 vulnerable people will be supported with FSL activities that will improve access to agricultural inputs and improved Animal Health, as well as specific activities aimed at crop protection.ltbrgtLastly, under the leadership of NADA, the Consortium will provide an integrated GBV, CP and GP response to conflict-affected communities in Tawilla locality.ltbrgtlt/pgt
